colorSpaceCompare.knowledgeTitle: Choose the color space that fits the task
colorSpaceCompare.knowledgeIntro: Use HSL, HSV, and OKLCH to create and adjust colors; Lab and LCh to compare them; gamut checks to confirm output; and RGB, HEX, or CMYK for different delivery workflows.

knowledge.rgbBody: These are the most common formats for websites, apps, and developer handoff. HEX is only a hexadecimal notation for sRGB values, not a separate color space, and is convenient for final delivery.
knowledge.hslBody: HSL makes theme states approachable through hue, saturation, and lightness; HSV mirrors many familiar color pickers. Both are intuitive, but equal numeric steps are not perceptually equal.
knowledge.okBody: OKLCH offers direct control over lightness, chroma, and hue for brand scales and dark mode. OKLab is useful for interpolation and comparison. High-chroma colors still need a gamut check.
knowledge.labBody: Lab is widely used in measurement and imaging workflows; LCh is its more intuitive cylindrical form. This tool uses D65, while CSS lab() / lch() default to D50, so their values are not interchangeable.
knowledge.cmykBody: This unprofiled generic formula is only a first look at ink components. Real output depends on paper, ink, the press, and an ICC profile, so it cannot replace a print proof.
knowledge.gamutBody: Gamut status describes the source color. Outside sRGB, the preview and RGB-family values are channel-clipped while the original OKLab / Lab values remain; this is not professional ICC gamut mapping.

hardwareOverviewPage.title: System Overview
hardwareOverviewPage.subtitle: Read local system and core hardware information. Nothing is uploaded.
hardwareOverviewPage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open System Overview in ToolKnit Desktop to read local hardware information.
hardwareOverviewPage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
hardwareOverviewPage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never uploads or changes system configuration.
hardwareOverviewPage.statusSecureBootOff: Secure Boot is not enabled. This can be normal on older hardware or dual-boot systems.
hardwareOverviewPage.statusTpmUnavailable: No usable TPM was detected. This can occur on older devices or when firmware TPM is disabled.
hardwareOverviewPage.statusNoBattery: No battery was detected, which is normal for most desktop computers.

cpuMemoryPage.title: CPU & Memory
cpuMemoryPage.subtitle: Read local processor specifications, memory topology, and current resource usage.
cpuMemoryPage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open CPU & Memory in ToolKnit Desktop to read local hardware information.
cpuMemoryPage.readFailedTitle: CPU and memory information is unavailable
cpuMemoryPage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
cpuMemoryPage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never uploads or changes system configuration.
cpuMemoryPage.statusVirtualizationOn: Firmware virtualization is enabled for Hyper-V, WSL, and virtual machine software.
cpuMemoryPage.statusVirtualizationOff: The processor supports virtualization, but firmware virtualization is disabled or unavailable.
cpuMemoryPage.statusFrequencyInfo: Current and reported memory frequencies are shown separately. XMP or EXPO profiles are never inferred from a model name.

gpuDisplayPage.title: GPU & Displays
gpuDisplayPage.subtitle: Read local graphics adapters, drivers, video memory, and connected display information.
gpuDisplayPage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open GPU & Displays in ToolKnit Desktop to read local hardware information.
gpuDisplayPage.readFailedTitle: Graphics and display information is unavailable
gpuDisplayPage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
gpuDisplayPage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never uploads or changes display configuration.
gpuDisplayPage.statusDxgi: Dedicated video memory is read through Windows DXGI instead of the legacy WMI field that truncates large GPUs.
gpuDisplayPage.statusVirtual: Virtual display adapters are listed separately and never replace the physical primary GPU.

mainboardPage.title: Mainboard & Firmware
mainboardPage.subtitle: Read local mainboard, BIOS/UEFI, boot security capabilities, and PCI device information.
mainboardPage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open Mainboard & Firmware in ToolKnit Desktop to read local hardware information.
mainboardPage.readFailedTitle: Mainboard and firmware information is unavailable
mainboardPage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
mainboardPage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never uploads or changes firmware, Secure Boot, or device configuration.
mainboardPage.statusSecureBootOff: Secure Boot is not enabled. This can be normal on older hardware or dual-boot systems.
mainboardPage.statusTpmUnavailable: No usable TPM was detected. This can occur on older devices or when firmware TPM is disabled.
mainboardPage.statusVirtualizationOn: Firmware virtualization is enabled for Hyper-V, WSL, and virtual machine software.
mainboardPage.statusVirtualizationOff: The processor supports virtualization, but firmware virtualization is disabled or unavailable.

storagePage.title: Storage & Health
storagePage.subtitle: Read local physical disks, volume capacity, and reliability counters provided by Windows.
storagePage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open Storage & Health in ToolKnit Desktop to read local storage information.
storagePage.readFailedTitle: Storage and health information is unavailable
storagePage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
storagePage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never runs SMART scans, repair, TRIM, or any write operation.
storagePage.statusHealthy: Windows reports that all identified physical disks are healthy.
storagePage.statusAttention: At least one disk or volume needs attention. Back up important files before checking system warnings.
storagePage.statusReliability: Reliability counters depend on disk, controller, and driver support. Missing fields are never inferred.
storagePage.statusSpace: {count} local volumes have less than 15% free space. Consider cleaning up or expanding capacity.

networkDevicesPage.title: Network & Devices
networkDevicesPage.subtitle: Read local network, Bluetooth, audio, USB, and camera device status without exposing network addresses.
networkDevicesPage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open Network & Devices in ToolKnit Desktop to read local device information.
networkDevicesPage.readFailedTitle: Network and device information is unavailable
networkDevicesPage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
networkDevicesPage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never displays or uploads IP, MAC, Bluetooth address, or other network identifiers.
networkDevicesPage.statusNetworkInactive: No connected network adapter is currently detected.
networkDevicesPage.statusDevices: Device lists are grouped by name, manufacturer, and status so system service entries do not repeat across the page.

powerSensorsPage.title: Power & Sensors
powerSensorsPage.subtitle: Read the active power plan, battery state, and temperature or fan sensors actually exposed by firmware.
powerSensorsPage.desktopOnlyDesc: Open Power & Sensors in ToolKnit Desktop to read local power and sensor information.
powerSensorsPage.readFailedTitle: Power and sensor information is unavailable
powerSensorsPage.readFailedDesc: Windows did not return a complete result. Please refresh and try again.
powerSensorsPage.statusReadOnly: All information is read locally. ToolKnit never changes power plans, firmware, fan policy, or battery configuration.
powerSensorsPage.statusBatteryHealthy: Full charge capacity looks healthy compared with design capacity.
powerSensorsPage.statusBatteryAttention: Full charge capacity is much lower than design capacity. Battery wear may need attention.
powerSensorsPage.statusBatteryUnknown: A battery was detected, but Windows did not provide design or full-charge capacity. Health is not inferred.
powerSensorsPage.statusNoBattery: No battery was detected. This is normal on desktops or systems that do not expose a battery interface.
powerSensorsPage.statusThermal: ACPI thermal zones come from firmware interfaces and are not CPU/GPU core temperatures. Missing fields are never inferred.
powerSensorsPage.statusNoFans: Windows did not provide fan sensor data. Many motherboards do not expose fan speed through standard Windows interfaces.
